```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(NatureCubeR)
```

This document describes the core project-data workflow in `NatureCubeR`:
authenticating, browsing your project's sensors and media, and managing
species labels.

## What the workflow does

- Confirms the active project using your API key
- Retrieves sensor/station metadata as a spatial (`sf`) object
- Plots station locations on an interactive map
- Fetches media assets for one or more stations
- Browses, searches and pulls species labels (project and IUCN)
- Pushes labels back to the platform
- Marks segments blank and publishes them

> **Steps 6 and 7 write to the platform.** Try them on one or two segments
> first.

---

## Prerequisites

Set your credentials in `~/.Renviron` and restart R:

```
NATURECUBE_API_KEY=your_api_key_here
NATURECUBE_URL=https://naturecube.io/api/
```

See `tutorials/auth_tutorial.Rmd` for full authentication details.

---

## Step 1 — Authenticate

```{r auth, eval=FALSE}
api_key <- get_key()
hdr <- auth_headers(api_key)
```

---

## Step 2 — Confirm the active project

```{r project, eval=FALSE}
get_project(hdr = hdr)
```

Prints the project name associated with your API key. There is no return
value.

---

## Step 3 — Retrieve station metadata and plot locations

```{r stations, eval=FALSE}
stations <- get_station_info(hdr = hdr, datatype = "image")
names(stations)

plot_stations(stations)
```

`get_station_info()` returns an `sf` object with one row per sensor
deployment. `datatype` accepts `"video"`, `"audio"`, `"image"`, or `"eDNA"`.
The columns used in the next step are `project_system_record_id` (the station
ID the media functions need) and `record_count` (the number of media files).
The table also holds `device_id` and the deployment start and end timestamps.

`plot_stations()` renders an interactive leaflet map with circle markers sized
by `record_count`.

---

## Step 4 — Fetch media assets

`get_media_assets()` takes the station IDs in `psrID`. Pass `record_count`
as well so stations with no media are skipped without an API call.

Start with a single station to see what comes back:

```{r media-one, eval=FALSE}
first_station <- which(stations$record_count > 0)[1]

media_one <- get_media_assets(
  hdr          = hdr,
  datatype     = "image",
  psrID        = stations$project_system_record_id[first_station],
  record_count = stations$record_count[first_station]
)
names(media_one)   # includes segment_record_id and media_file_record_id
```

Then fetch every station in the project:

```{r media-all, eval=FALSE}
media_assets <- get_media_assets(
  hdr          = hdr,
  datatype     = "image",
  psrID        = stations$project_system_record_id,
  record_count = stations$record_count,
  max_workers  = 4L
)
```

The result is a tibble with one row per media segment, including
`segment_record_id` and `media_file_record_id`. Each station is paged until
the API returns an empty page.

About `max_workers`:

- Up to `max_workers` stations are downloaded at once (default `4`).
- The API answers HTTP 429 when it is asked for too much. The function waits
  and retries on its own; if you still see 429s, lower `max_workers`.
- `max_workers = 1L` downloads one station at a time in the current R
  session. Above 1, the stations are fetched by background R processes that
  load the **installed** NatureCubeR, not code loaded with
  `devtools::load_all()`. Use `max_workers = 1L` while developing the package.

---

## Step 5 — Browse and manage species labels

### 5a — Project labels

```{r project-labels, eval=FALSE}
project_labels <- get_project_labels(hdr = hdr, labeltype = "Camera")
names(project_labels)
```

Returns the species labels currently available to labellers on the dashboard.
`labeltype` is `"Camera"` or `"Bioacoustic"`; pass exactly one.

### 5b — Search the IUCN database

```{r iucn-search, eval=FALSE}
horse <- getIUCNLabels(hdr = hdr, offset = 0, search_term = "Domestic horse")

horse$data    # the rows on this page
horse$total   # rows matching the search across all pages
```

`getIUCNLabels()` returns **one page of up to 1000 rows**. The page size is
fixed, so there is no `limit` argument; use `offset` to move through the
results. The list also holds `$offset` and `$limit`.

### 5c — Pull the whole database, or one taxonomic group

Omit `search_term` and keep asking for the next page until you have `total`
rows. There is no server-side filter on class, order or family, so filter the
result afterwards:

```{r iucn-all, eval=FALSE}
pages <- list()
offset <- 0L
repeat {
  page <- getIUCNLabels(hdr = hdr, offset = offset)
  pages[[length(pages) + 1L]] <- page$data
  offset <- offset + nrow(page$data)
  if (nrow(page$data) == 0L || offset >= page$total) break
}
iucn_labels <- dplyr::bind_rows(pages)

# All birds. The rank column may be called `class` or `class_`; check with
# names(iucn_labels) and use whichever your data has.
class_col <- intersect(c("class", "class_"), names(iucn_labels))[1]
birds <- iucn_labels[iucn_labels[[class_col]] %in% "Aves", ]
```

### 5d — Add new IUCN species to the database

This writes to the shared label database. `chunksize` must be smaller than
the number of rows.

```{r iucn-add, eval=FALSE}
# Prepare a data frame with the required IUCN columns, then upload in chunks.
# example_data <- readLines("path/to/species.json") %>% jsonlite::fromJSON()
# example_data$extant_country_list <- NA
# add_IUCN_labels(hdr = hdr, labels = example_data, chunksize = 500)
```

---

## Step 6 — Push labels back to the platform

Build one row per media segment you want to label. `push_new_labels()` renames
`segment_record_id` to `segment_record_id_fk` and `label_id` to `label_id_fk`
for you, so use the names exactly as they appear in `media_assets` and
`project_labels`.

```{r push-labels, eval=FALSE}
label_common_name <- "Uneven-toothed Rat"   # a common_name from project_labels
new_label_id <- project_labels$label_id[
  which(project_labels$common_name == label_common_name)
]
stopifnot(length(new_label_id) == 1L)

submission_frame <- data.frame(
  segment_record_id     = media_assets$segment_record_id[1],
  label_id              = new_label_id,
  number_of_individuals = 1L
)

push_new_labels(hdr = hdr, submission_records = submission_frame, chunksize = 30)
```

`chunksize` controls how many records are sent per API request. Optional
columns are `label_record_uuid`, `prediction_accuracy`, `label_created_at` and
`label_record_id`; any other column is rejected before anything is sent.

---

## Step 7 — Mark segments blank and publish them

```{r blank-publish, eval=FALSE}
segment_ids <- media_assets$segment_record_id[1:2]

# Mark the labels on these segments as blank (TRUE) or undo it (FALSE).
set_segment_blank_status(hdr, blank_status = TRUE, segment_record_ids = segment_ids)

# Publish (TRUE) or unpublish (FALSE) segment records, in chunks of
# `chunksize` IDs per request (default 500).
publish_segments(hdr, publish_status = TRUE, segment_record_ids = segment_ids)
```
